insight: Iran's performance in the 2026 FIFA World Cup shows a notable impact from hydration breaks, with the team gaining momentum in 4 out of 6 breaks, resulting in a slight increase in their overall pace. This suggests that the breaks allowed Iran to regroup and come back stronger, with an average increase in pace of 0.050 minutes per break. However, when Iran was pressing before a hydration break, they tended to lose momentum, with their pace decreasing by an average of 0.100 minutes per break, and they were unable to regain their momentum after the break in either of these instances. In contrast, when Iran was not pressing before a break, they were able to maintain and even increase their pace, with an average increase of 0.125 minutes per break, indicating that the breaks provided a much-needed opportunity for the team to recharge and refocus.
